Chapter 7: The Gentle Art of Letting Go.
You know, holding on—that’s the easy part. But letting go? Especially when it comes to control, expectations, or even old hurts—that’s a whole different story. Funny thing is, it’s often the act of letting go that brings us the most peace. And Piglet, in his own gentle way, really shows us what it means to trust the unfolding of things.
Imagine a parent watching their child grow up. There’s this natural instinct to protect, to guide every little step, to hold on just a bit tighter. But eventually, every parent realizes that real love means letting go—letting their child stumble, make mistakes, and discover their own path. It’s bittersweet, isn’t it? And yet, there’s a kind of freedom in that release.
Piglet faces this in his own way. He’s often anxious, always worrying about what could go wrong, wishing for things to be safe and predictable. But life in the Hundred Acre Wood? It’s full of surprises. Plans fall apart, friends make mistakes, and sometimes, things just don’t turn out how you hoped. Bit by bit, Piglet learns to let go of his need for certainty. The moment he stops trying to control everything, he discovers he can actually relax—and even enjoy the moment.
There’s this one story where Piglet loses something precious to him. At first, he’s devastated—searching everywhere, retracing his steps, hoping to find what’s missing. But as he slowly lets go of the search, he starts to notice the comfort of his friends around him. The loss doesn’t magically disappear, but it gets lighter, a little easier to bear. By letting go, Piglet finds he’s made space for new joys to enter his life.
Most of us don’t realize just how much energy we spend holding on—whether it’s to old grudges, rigid plans, or the way things “should” be. But when you start to let go, something wonderful happens. You discover a new kind of freedom. Life stops being about controlling every outcome, and starts being about trust.
Piglet’s journey is a gentle reminder that letting go isn’t giving up. It’s about making room for what really matters—connection, being present, and finding peace. The world is always changing. The more we’re able to flow with it, the happier we become.
